title: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm
authors: Carlos Bravo-Prieto, Aram W. Harrow, Robin Kothari
abstract: In the quantum linear systems problem (QLSP), we are given query access to a $d$-sparse $N\times N$ matrix $A$ with condition number $κ$, and the ability to prepare a quantum state proportional to a vector $\vec b$. The goal is to output an $ε$-approximation to the quantum state proportional to the solution $\vec x$ of $A\vec{x}=\vec{b}$. Following a long line of work, the best previously known quantum algorithms for the QLSP had query complexities $O(κd\log(1/ε))$ and $κ\sqrt d(κd/ε)^{o(1)}$, while the best known lower bounds were $Ω(κ\log(1/ε))$ and $Ω(κ\sqrt d)$. We improve these bounds and show that the complexity of the QLSP is $Θ(κ\sqrt d\log(1/ε))$. We also resolve an open problem of Berry and Childs by showing that any $N\times N$ unitary can be implemented with bounded error using $O(\sqrt N)$ queries to its matrix entries.
summary: This paper determines the optimal quantum query complexity for solving the Quantum Linear Systems Problem (QLSP) to be $\Theta(\kappa \sqrt{d} \log(1/\epsilon))$. The authors achieve this by developing a sophisticated block encoding technique and simultaneously proving the matching lower bound by embedding a known hard problem into the QLSP structure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the Quantum Linear Systems Problem (QLSP): finding an approximation to the solution vector $\vec{x}$ for the equation $A\vec{x}=\vec{b}$ given quantum query access to the sparse matrix $A$.
main_result: The authors establish the optimal query complexity for the QLSP to be $\Theta(\kappa \sqrt{d} \log(1/\epsilon))$, matching the best known lower bounds.
method: The upper bound is achieved by reducing the QLSP to solving a larger linear system via a block encoding construction, which is implemented using $O(1)$ queries to the sparse-matrix oracle.
model_or_system: The analysis is based on the abstract mathematical model of quantum query complexity, involving sparse matrices $A$ (with condition number $\kappa$ and sparsity $d$), and the ability to prepare quantum states proportional to $\vec{b}$.
key_observables: Query complexity, approximation error $\epsilon$, condition number $\kappa$, and matrix sparsity $d$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes access to standard sparse-matrix oracles and utilizes the model developed by Childs, Kothari, and Somma.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the QLSP and reviews prior bounds. It then presents the main result (Theorem 1) establishing the $\Theta(\kappa \sqrt{d} \log(1/\epsilon))$ complexity. The methodology involves constructing a block encoding for a larger system and deriving the lower bound by embedding a hard problem (related to $FR,D$) into the QLSP instance.
why_interesting: The work provides a fundamental, optimal complexity result for a cornerstone problem in quantum computation, directly impacting the theoretical limits of quantum simulation and quantum machine learning algorithms.
